subject: neovate-code
title: ACP always-allow is cached per toolName:category and replayed without re-consulting the tool's per-command risk logic, so one grant admits every later bash call including banned ones
evidence: src/commands/acp/session.ts:113-119 (ruleKey = `${toolName}:${category}`), :131-137 (cached decision returned without prompting); risk lives only in tools' needsApproval (src/tools/bash.ts:975-990) which is short-circuited by the cached rule
one_why: Converges with the coarse-grant cluster (cf. kolega prefix-rule bypass): a category is not a grant unit for bash because risk is a function of the command string; the cache must key on command atom, or at minimum re-run needsApproval for high-risk/banned commands even when a category grant exists.

subject: neovate-code
title: Prune-before-summarize: LLM-free tool-output pruning with recency budget, protected tools, and minimum-prune hysteresis, re-measured before escalating to compaction
evidence: src/history.ts:268-300 (step-1 prune, re-check usage, step-2 LLM compact only if still overflowing), src/compression.ts:127-212 (reverse walk, protectTurns=2, protected tools skill/task, 40k recency budget, stop-at-pruned sentinel, >=20k minimum prune), src/constants.ts:101-105
one_why: The re-measure between tiers is the port: most tiered designs fire both tiers from a stale estimate; hysteresis (skip prune unless >=20k freed) prevents churn on borderline sessions; pruned parts keep a prunedAt marker that doubles as the walk-stop sentinel.

subject: neovate-code
title: Turn cap deflated by tool calls: turnsCount -= approvedToolUses.length makes tool-heavy loops effectively unbounded against max_turns
evidence: src/loop.ts:736-737 (turnsCount decremented by number of approved tool uses each turn), cap check src/loop.ts:214-224 (max_turns default 50)
one_why: A model emitting 2 tool calls per turn never consumes budget (1-2=-1), so the only loop guard is disabled exactly in the scenario loops happen; with no loop-identity detection anywhere in the repo, a stuck same-call loop runs until API cost or the user stops it - budgets should count LLM turns only, never be negative-credited.

subject: neovate-code
title: Bash policy is best-of-species among deny-lists (pipeline-segment evaluation credited to codex PR #7544, command-substitution rejection with tested quoting edge cases) but still root-name matching that python -c or find -exec trivially bypasses
evidence: src/tools/bash.ts:18-43 (24 banned roots incl rm/curl/sh), :248-273 (pipeline segment fallback), :283-287 (hasCommandSubstitution reject), tests src/tools/bash.test.ts:14-79
one_why: The banned list only raises needsApproval (bash.ts:975-990) so it fails toward human review, not execution block - which is the honest role for a denylist; but nothing prompts in yolo, and command substitution is rejected outright rather than flagged, an odd asymmetry worth converging with the grammar-parsed-bash-policy cluster.

subject: neovate-code
title: Prompt-cache breakpoints are a static heuristic: model-name substring match (claude|sonnet|opus) gating ephemeral marks on first-2-system + last-2-non-system messages, sliding every turn and never firing for other cache-capable providers
evidence: src/promptCache.ts:12-15 (shouldCache string includes-check), :26-28 (toCache = 2 system + last 2 non-system), applied each turn src/loop.ts:254
one_why: Converges with prompt-cache-marking: capability should come from the provider/model manifest (this repo already has a 1160-LOC modelMap.ts with per-model limit data), and the last-2-messages breakpoint invalidates itself each turn rather than using stable rolling breakpoints one turn apart (kolega pattern) - design-doc 2025-11-12-anthropic-prompt-caching.md shows the team knows, code is still v1.

subject: neovate-code
title: Every product surface - Ink TUI, programmatic SDK, ACP server, web+websocket server - is a thin client of one typed MessageBus/HandlerMap RPC contract generated via api-extractor, with handler slices registered per domain
evidence: src/nodeBridge.ts:3-19 (16 registerXxxHandlers slices), src/nodeBridge.types.ts:1-60 (generated HandlerMap), src/sdk.ts:27-33 (SDKClient = bus.request typed by HandlerMap), src/commands/server/websocketTransport.ts, src/uiBridge.ts:56 (TUI answers toolApproval on the same bus)
one_why: Cheapest full-surface fan-out seen: one loop, zero process boundaries in-process, yet the same request/response contract serializes over websocket for remote hosts; the 1930-LOC generated type file is the seam that keeps UI/SDK/ACP from accreting private copies of core logic (contrast nanocoder's per-entry-path re-implementations).

subject: neovate-code
title: Skills expose only name+description in the tool description; bodies are read at invocation, and the installer can target Claude's skill directories for cross-harness skill sharing
evidence: src/tools/skill.ts:8-27 (metadata-only <available_skills> rendering), :44-56 (readSkillBody on invoke), src/skill.ts:732-741 (SkillSource.GlobalClaude/ProjectClaude), src/commands/skill.tsx:632-650 (--claude install flags)
one_why: Converges with seeded lazy-skill-loading; the nuance worth taking is the interop posture - skills are written once and installed into .claude/skills or ~/.claude/skills so a rival harness reads the same packages, an unusually concrete cross-harness import path in either direction.
